title.en: Tropical Evergreen & Semi-Evergreen Forests of India

content.en: Multi-layered, high-density forest biomes found in regions of high precipitation and warm temperatures, exhibiting zero synchronized leaf-fall and exceptional biodiversity.
content.hi: Multi-layered, high-density forest biomes found in regions of high precipitation and warm temperatures, exhibiting zero synchronized leaf-fall and exceptional biodiversity.

content.en:
• Climatic Conditions: Annual rainfall > 200 cm, average temperature 22°C–27°C, high humidity (> 70%).
• Distribution in India: Western slopes of Western Ghats, hills of North-Eastern states (Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Tripura), and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
• Stratification: Four distinct vertical tiers: ground layer/ferns, shrubs, sub-canopy, and dense continuous canopy with emergent trees reaching heights > 60m.
• Key Species: Rosewood, Mahogany, Ebony, Aini, Semul, Bamboo, Mesua, Agarwood.
• Tropical Semi-Evergreen Forests: Transitional zones receiving 150-200 cm rainfall; mixture of evergreen and moist deciduous species (e.g. White cedar, Holock, Champa).
